messages:
maya (support): heads up — several hosted API customers reporting 5xx / timeouts starting ~2026-03-15T11:03:00Z. Customers see 502/504 and some 500s with 'upstream read timeout'. Example response from gateway: 

{
  "error": "upstream timeout",
  "status": 504,
  "correlation_id": "cid_0x7f9a2b3c"
}

Attached request sample: 
`curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX" -H "X-Request-Id: cid_0x7f9a2b3c" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`

We have customer repro steps and logs. Root cause looks like the KV/prefix cache (redis) is throwing connection errors -> cache misses -> huge spike to inference runtime -> timeouts. Raising for triage and quick mitigation.

monitoring-bot: ALERT: redwood.cache.errors high (prod)
- window: 11:02-11:08 UTC
- cache error rate: 68% (baseline 0.2%)
- avg gateway 5xx: 420/min
- affected routes: /v1/generate (heavy prefix caching), /v1/chat/stream
- alert link: https://mon.redwood.ai/alerts/INC-2035

sam (eng-oncall): @jia @pat please confirm — do we have redis/memcached for prefix KVs in hosted? Which cluster?

jia (eng-runtime): yes — hosted uses redis-cluster-prod-1 for prefix/KV caching (prefix-caching daemon = kv-cache-proxy). Seeing many `ERR max number of clients reached` and `read tcp ... connection reset by peer` in kv-cache-proxy logs starting 11:01 UTC. Example kv-cache-proxy log snippet: 

```
2026-03-15T11:01:12Z kv-cache-proxy ERROR redis.Do: dial tcp 10.8.3.45:6379: connect: connection refused
2026-03-15T11:01:17Z kv-cache-proxy ERROR redis.Do: ERR max number of clients reached
2026-03-15T11:01:18Z kv-cache-proxy WARN cache miss fallback -> backend
```
Looks like either connection exhaustion on redis or a networking flake between cache-proxy and redis. Misses ballooned -> inference runtime got a stampede of cold requests and started timing out.

pat (eng-platform): checking infra changes — there was a config push at 10:50 UTC that increased client-concurrency in kv-cache-proxy from 1000 -> 5000 to optimize throughput for embeddings. Might have exposed maxclients on redis set to 4096. Sending redis team note.

tom_cs: impacted customers have opened escalations: AcmeCorp, FathomAI, Plexity. CS notified and asked for an ETA. I'll draft customer blurb once we have mitigation.

sam (eng-oncall): action plan:
1) immediate mitigation: flip prefix-caching to bypass for heavy routes (feature flag) so we stop pressure on redis and let requests hit runtime uncached but with rate-limiters.
2) scale redis-cluster (or increase maxclients) + restart redis-primary if needed.
3) roll back the 10:50 config change to kv-cache-proxy if it keeps hammering redis.

Can someone run the bypass flag now?

jia (eng-runtime): running quick bypass now — setting `feature.prefix_cache_enabled=false` for hosted API routes `/v1/generate` and `/v1/chat/*` (will be a controlled toggle). Command: 

# service control
rwctl feature-toggle set prefix_cache_enabled false --scope hosted --routes "/v1/generate,/v1/chat/*"

deploy-bot: feature toggle applied by jia at 2026-03-15T11:06:43Z (id: ft-9091) — toggled prefix_cache_enabled=false for scope=hosted routes=`/v1/generate,/v1/chat/*`.

monitoring-bot: metrics update 11:07 UTC:
- cache error rate dropped from 68% -> 12% (after partial bypass)
- gateway 5xx rate dropping, but still elevated: 150/min
- backend qlen (inference-runtime) high: 360 -> need more capacity or graceful queueing

sam (eng-oncall): good. Next: can infra scale redis or bump maxclients? pat?

pat (eng-platform): redis team recommends bumping `maxclients` from 4096 -> 8192 and adding one failover replica to reduce client churn. Doing a rolling config change + sentinel failover prep. I will schedule a rolling restart on redis-primary after config change to apply. ETA ~ 12 minutes.

jia (eng-runtime): note — while redis is unhealthy we should also rate-limit long-running streaming sessions to avoid runtime queue buildup. I'll lower default streaming concurrency for hosted from 10 -> 4. Pushing config now.

deploy-bot: redis-config patch applied to cluster redis-cluster-prod-1 (patch id cfg-233), will perform rolling restart in 2m.

pagerbot: scheduled maintenance: restarting redis nodes in rolling fashion (nodes: r1,r2,r3) starting 11:18 UTC. Pager duty oncall: @sam.

deploy-bot: restart of redis-primary (r1) started 11:18:32Z — restarting process (docker svc restart redis-server).

deploy-bot: restart complete r1 11:20:01Z. r2 restart started 11:20:30Z.

monitoring-bot: post-restart metrics 11:24 UTC:
- redis connections stable ~ 4500 (below new max)
- cache error rate ~ 4%
- gateway 5xx: 12/min (almost back to baseline)
- inference-runtime qlen decreasing to 40

sam (eng-oncall): confirm if traffic fully recovered and no more customer 5xx reports.

maya (support): AcmeCorp confirmed errors stopped at ~11:25 UTC. Plexity reports degraded performance but no 5xx. FathomAI: reporting one remaining 502 at 11:28 (cid_0x7f9a2b3c-2).

jia (eng-runtime): I will roll back the bypass after redis health is green and we finish config validation. Plan: re-enable prefix_cache after 30m of stable metrics and slowly ramp concurrency back.

tom_cs: drafted customer message for impacted customers:
"We experienced a degradation in our prefix caching layer which caused elevated 5xx/timeouts for the hosted API. We mitigated the issue by bypassing the prefix cache and scaling the Redis cluster; normal service was restored at 11:25 UTC. We are performing a postmortem and will follow up with root cause and permanent remediation."

sam (eng-oncall): postmortem notes / immediate follow-ups:
- revert the 10:50 change that increased client concurrency until we've validated redis capacity and connection pooling (pat).
- add autoscaling on redis-connections and an alert when `redis.connected_clients / redis.maxclients > 0.8` (monitoring-bot).
- add circuit-breaker in kv-cache-proxy to return 429 instead of falling back to origin when redis health is degraded, to avoid stampedes (jia).
- schedule postmortem doc and RCA (owner: jia, due EOD).

pagerbot: incident INC-2035 created by maya at 2026-03-15T11:05:12Z. Severity: P1. Incident channel: #incidents-2035.

maya (support): closing loop with customers now; I'll post the PS and follow up once the RCA is done. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

jia (eng-runtime): quick note for RCA: suspect low redis `maxclients` combined with aggressive kv-cache-proxy concurrency bump. Might also be an underlying network flake between AZs — collecting tcpdump and redis slowlogs.

sam (eng-oncall): thanks team. please add any logs/traces to INC-2035 and ping when the postmortem is ready.

monitoring-bot: INC-2035 status -> resolved (11:30 UTC) — metrics stable for 5 minutes.

maya (support): resolved for now. will keep thread updated if anything else pops up.
